notes.heading: State whether the result is a match or an insertion position
paragraphs: Search contracts determine how equality and boundaries should be handled. A routine that returns any matching index is different from one that returns the first matching index or the first value at least as large as a target. Half-open bounds [low,high) can simplify insertion-position searches: high may equal the list length without being read as an element. A loop must shrink the interval on every iteration. Trace absent targets and duplicates as well as successful matches, and retain original indices if sorting would otherwise lose them.

questions.prompt: Find the first index with value at least 5 in sorted [1,3,3,7,9] using low=0, high=5, while low<high, mid=floor((low+high)/2), low=mid+1 if a[mid]<5, otherwise high=mid. Trace mid and return low.
solution: At 2, value 3 moves low to 3; at 4, value 9 moves high to 4.
At 3, value 7 moves high to 3 and the interval becomes empty.

questions.prompt: Using the same half-open lower-bound contract on [2,4,6] for target 9, what index is returned and why must it not be dereferenced?
questions.answer: Return 3, the list length. It represents insertion after all elements and is not a valid existing element index.
solution: Every stored value is less than 9, so the lower bound is the end position.
Distinguish a valid insertion position from a valid array element.

questions.prompt: An unsorted list is [30,10,20]. An application sorts it and finds 20 at sorted index 1, then reports original index 1. Explain and repair the error.
questions.answer: 20 was originally at index 2. Store value-original-index pairs before sorting, or use linear search on the original list.
solution: Sorting changes positions while leaving values intact.
Carry original indices through the transformation when the contract requires them.
markingPoints: Give a valid preservation or search method.
